chunks.heading: The Knife I Chose
chunks.notes: She flees an unnamed threat into the arms of a "familiar, steady" figure who then knifes her, landing the poem's explicit "trust has teeth" line.

chunks.heading: The Knife I Chose
chunks.notes: She realizes "the knife was always there" yet clings to her betrayer rather than face the night alone, culminating in a surrendering kiss.

chunks.heading: The Knife I Chose
chunks.notes: She survives but the poem explicitly reframes the event as "not an ending, but an inheritance... repeated like a sacred curse," closing on a stated cyclical/generational pattern of love and ruin.
